reasoning_traces.think:
Shannon entropy provides a fundamental measure of information content in a random variable, defined as the expected value of the negative logarithm of its probability. It forms the basis for mutual information, which quantifies dependence between variables. KL divergence extends this by comparing two probability distributions, offering insight into how much information is lost when one distribution is used to approximate another. These primitives underpin both GSI’s Bayesian inference framework—where entropy guides prior construction and KL helps assess model fit—and GSE’s state-transition modeling, where mutual information captures dependencies among system components and KL divergence evaluates policy performance under uncertainty.
